report:
The entire supplied partial manuscript is mathematically sound within its stated restrictions. This verdict does not validate the original dossier’s prior assertions or close original P05.1/P05.2. No caller mathematical grants, ledger verdicts, compilation results, hashes, or visual flags were used as evidence.

I opened the literal versioned [BMPS v1 PDF](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.08664v1). I read complete Definitions 2.1–2.4, 2.18–2.31, 3.1–3.3, 3.14, 3.20, 3.23 and 4.4, Definition 2.13, and the entire Lemma 2.24 proof. The external entries below concern source conventions and scope; the new mathematical conclusions were independently reconstructed. Neither automatic continuity nor any general regularization, positivity, contact, or extended Monge–Ampère theorem is imported.

For the height identity, saturation gives N_tau = N_sigma intersect span_R(tau−tau). Thus N_sigma/N_tau is torsion-free of rank one. A lattice basis of N_tau followed by an inward primitive lift is a basis of N_sigma. Its volume is a_tau times the perpendicular height, proving pi_tau(n_sigma/tau) = (a_sigma/a_tau) nu_sigma/tau. Projecting lattice balancing and multiplying by a_tau gives sum_sigma w_sigma a_sigma nu_sigma/tau = 0. Consequently the Euclidean weights MULTIPLY: c_sigma = w_sigma a_sigma. Using w_sigma/a_sigma would generally fail. Saturation of the lattice generated collectively by the fan’s rays is unnecessary; the argument uses each saturated tangent lattice separately.

For stationarity, intrinsic divergence is the divergence of the orthogonal tangential projection of the ambient field. Its outward flux is Y paired with minus the inward unit conormal. Truncating each unbounded polyhedron by a sufficiently large box places every artificial boundary outside the field’s support, so its flux is zero. The bounded-polyhedron formula follows by triangulation and the fundamental theorem of calculus; artificial internal simplex facets cancel. Genuine facets then cancel by the height identity, even when adjacent top cells have different tangent planes. Intersections of lower dimension contribute no facet measure. In dimension one, facet measure is counting measure and the contributions are endpoint values; they are retained and cancelled, not discarded. Full affine linear cells require no genuine boundary contributions. All integrals are finite because the field has compact support.

The compact-support contradiction is valid only for the finite globally embedded support in one vector space. Under the hypothesized compactness, every cell is bounded. A smooth compactly supported field equal to x near the support has tangential divergence d on every top cell. Every top cell has strictly positive finite relative d-volume, and every c_sigma is strictly positive. Therefore 0 = d sum_sigma c_sigma vol_d(sigma) contradicts positivity. This excludes nonempty positive-dimensional compact supports in that category. It does not exclude an abstract compact balanced space, establish balancing of a bounded skeleton at its boundary, or apply the same argument across toric strata.

The fan proof also checks. The cutoff field is smooth at the origin because its radial factor is constant near zero. On each cone, x lies in its tangent space, giving div_sigma(b chi(|x|)) = chi'(|x|) times <b,x>/|x|. Polar integration is performed separately in each d-dimensional tangent space. The radial factor is finite and strictly negative; for d=1 it is exactly −1 and the angular integral uses the two-point sphere with counting measure. Common lineality and full linear cones cause no extra boundary term. A linear form nonnegative on the support and positive at a point is positive on a relatively open angular portion of an incident top cone, of positive angular measure, contradicting the zero weighted angular barycenter.

The finite-generation and separation steps admit elementary reconstruction. Quotient a rational cone by its rational lineality and choose a rational complement. For the resulting pointed cone, the sum of its defining nonnegative linear forms is strictly positive away from zero. Its level-one slice is a bounded rational polytope. A nonvertex point splits along a direction preserving its active equations into boundary points; induction on face dimension expresses it through vertices. Vertices solve independent rational equations, hence are rational. Adding a rational lineality basis and its negatives therefore gives finite rational generators. A finitely generated cone is closed: eliminate dependent active generators in any nonnegative representation; along a convergent sequence, pass to a fixed independent active set, whose coefficients converge by an invertible minor. If q is outside this closed convex cone, its nearest point p exists. For u=p−q, the projection inequality gives <u,k−p> ≥ 0 for every cone point k; testing 0 and 2p gives <u,p>=0. Hence <u,k> ≥ 0 and <u,q>=−|u|²<0. This supplies the required separator. Since the support spans L, a nonzero separator on L would be positive somewhere on the support. Thus its generated cone is L.

The strictly positive rational relation does not depend on rational top weights. For each chosen nonzero cone generator v_i, −v_i has a nonnegative representation by the chosen generators. If its active columns are dependent, choose a kernel vector h with a positive entry and subtract s h, where s is the minimum of coefficient_j/h_j over positive h_j. Coefficients remain nonnegative and at least one active column disappears. Iteration leaves independent rational columns. Their unique coefficients are rational by Gaussian elimination on an invertible rational minor. Summing the resulting relations v_i + sum_j b_ij v_j = 0 gives rational coefficients lambda_j = 1 + sum_i b_ij ≥ 1. This establishes positivity on every chosen generator without a rational-feasibility black box.

The maximum principle retains continuity throughout. At x in relint(tau), the active rational inequalities describe the local tangent cones; inactive inequalities impose no restriction on sufficiently short displacements. Faces containing tau correspond to star faces, with unchanged tangent spaces and saturated lattices. Facet quotients and inward signs are preserved, so inherited strictly positive weights balance the star. This independently confirms the pertinent local-star application, including common lineality along tau. At a rational maximum point, finitely many rational generators permit one common rational epsilon>0 with every z_i=x+epsilon v_i in its assigned incident face. Every incident rational y has a nonnegative conical representation y−x=sum_i a_i v_i. Choose t≥max_i(a_i/lambda_i). Setting beta_i=(t lambda_i−a_i)/epsilon gives (y−x)+sum_i beta_i(z_i−x)=0. Normalization produces a permitted PCC with coefficient 1/(1+sum_i beta_i)>0 at y. The global upper bound and Jensen force f(y) to equal the maximum. Rational density and continuity then extend equality to the incident faces.

For irrational maxima, rational-endpoint Jensen extends by continuity to ordinary convexity within each relative face. If p is a relative-interior maximum and q lies in that face, a short point on the opposite side of p expresses p as a convex combination with positive coefficient at q. The global upper bound forces equality at q. A rational relative-interior maximum therefore exists, and the rational argument gives a neighborhood of p in the maximum set. That set is open and closed, proving componentwise constancy. Dimension zero is separately valid because components are points. In the abstract local-chart clause, the declared rational, finite, pure, saturated, strictly positive balanced conventions remain essential: complete incident stars must balance near each center, chart weights must be compatible, local PCC inequalities must hold, and every endpoint used must remain inside the chart. Only the local portion of an incident face is used there. No global embedding of the abstract space is inferred or required.

The discontinuity counterexample is correct. Every allowed endpoint of f=0 on Q and −1 elsewhere has value zero, whereas every center has value at most zero. Thus every printed PCC inequality holds, including combinations with irrational coefficients and irrational centers. The function is nevertheless discontinuous everywhere. This refutes the printed automatic-continuity assertion under those definitions; it neither changes their endpoint convention nor claims a discontinuous envelope.

For the compact connected chart category, continuous PC competitors are constants, so their envelope under the continuous obstacle is exactly min_X(gamma+u). With the separately supplied finite BOUNDED rational cell decomposition compatible with charts, take a common bounded rational subdivision. An affine function on each bounded cell minimizes at a vertex; vertices are rational by independent rational active equations. Literal integral-affine slopes and rational constants give rational vertex values, hence a rational minimum. The constant envelope is genuine literal PA and PAPC: all its linear parts vanish, so divisor formula (2.32) gives zero against every cycle. Its constant nonincreasing approximating sequence supplies regularization directly. In positive dimension, its raw iterated-divisor measure and contact integral are zero. These operator conclusions belong to this finite-PA branch; no extended operator on arbitrary continuous functions or arbitrary abstract spaces is asserted. An envelope with unrestricted, possibly discontinuous competitors remains outside the conclusion.

For a finite globally embedded zero-dimensional space, incidence forces every PCC endpoint to be the center singleton. The literal envelope is therefore gamma+u pointwise, with rational values. The zero-fold product is the given weighted zero-cycle, rather than the zero measure, and the contact gap vanishes identically.

No substantive repair is required. Harmless wording clarification: in local charts, the proof’s closed-star conclusion means its portion inside the chart; the manuscript already explicitly confines endpoints there. The results remain scoped supporting geometry and continuous compact-envelope statements, not a candidate solution of the full original classification. Noncompact higher-dimensional real regularity/contact, operator-domain identification for unrestricted competitors, and the necessary-and-sufficient original P05.1/P05.2 classification remain unproved. The review used read-only primary-source retrieval; no shell, workspace mutation, private-stream inspection, feedback, or external contact occurred.
premises: BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 uses finite globally embedded rational complexes, assumes purity, sets N_sigma=N intersect span_R(sigma−sigma), and uses inward primitive facet-quotient lifts, rational balancing weights modulo facet tangents, and strictly positive top cycles (Definitions 2.1–2.4, 2.18–2.27; Remark 2.5).

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 PCCs have rational endpoints, arbitrary real nonnegative coefficients summing to one, center x=sum_i alpha_i x_i, and faces tau≤sigma_i containing x and x_i on some rational structure. Definition 3.3 imposes Jensen inequalities without explicitly requiring continuity (Definitions 3.2–3.3).

BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 defines literal PA by continuity, integral slopes and rational constants; PAPC by nonnegative divisors; PCreg by uniform reference-bounded PAPC approximation; and raw MA by f^d·[X] using divisor formula (2.32) (Definitions 2.28–2.31, 3.1, 3.14, 3.20, 3.23, 4.4).
BMPS arXiv:2603.08664v1 defines its compactification as closure in a tropical toric space with quotient-vector-space strata, rather than closure inside N_R (Definition 2.13).
